part_title: Amazon Q Developer for AWS and Coding Workflows
review_basis: Narration prepared from the AIF module 07 lesson map and historical/current product caveats. Original numbered WebP integrity is gated in workflow; image-by-image visual content review not independently completed in this session.

scenes.title: Amazon Q Developer
scenes.narration: Now move from workplace question answering to assisting people who build and operate AWS workloads. Amazon Q Developer can help explain AWS concepts, suggest implementation steps and interpret certain information about an AWS environment when it has appropriate access. Consider a learner asking why an Amazon E C two server cannot be reached. The assistant may suggest checking the security group, routing, instance status and relevant logs. The assistant is offering guidance, not performing a verified repair simply by answering. When an account aware feature is used, the user's AWS identity and granted permissions determine what context is available. Suggestions must be checked against the actual resource settings and the current service documentation. If a command would change infrastructure, read it carefully before running it; confirm the target account, Region and resource. A beginner should remember the distinction between an AI recommendation and an executed, authorized operation. Would you blindly run a generated command in production? No. First understand its effect and validate that it is appropriate.

scenes.title: AWS operations and costs
scenes.narration: A developer or cloud engineer may ask why costs increased after deploying a new application. An assistant can explain cost concepts and may use permitted billing or cost information to help investigate. But an explanation is only as reliable as the data it can access. For example, a sudden increase might come from a larger compute instance, higher storage usage or more requests. Start by checking the relevant billing period and service breakdown in AWS Billing and Cost Management or Cost Explorer. Distinguish estimated charges from finalized billing figures, and watch for differences in account, currency, credits or time window. The assistant should not invent an invoice amount when it has no actual data. An actionable workflow is to form a hypothesis, inspect the source metric, compare it with the previous period, and then decide what should change. Cost optimizations can affect reliability, so do not downsize infrastructure solely because a chatbot suggested it. Question: where should the final cost number come from? From the authorized AWS billing records.

scenes.title: AI code companion
scenes.narration: An AI coding companion can help with tasks such as explaining an unfamiliar function, suggesting a unit test, or drafting a small implementation. For a beginner, generated code is a starting point that must be understood, not a proven working application. Suppose the model produces a Python function that uploads an image to Amazon S3. Review which bucket it targets, how it obtains credentials, which error cases it handles and whether permissions are narrower than necessary. Then run automated tests and appropriate security or dependency checks. Models may generate outdated library names, unsafe command usage or code that behaves differently from the written request. A passing syntax check is not enough: test realistic inputs, permissions and failure conditions. Avoid placing secrets in prompts, source code or logs. Human code review matters because the developer remains responsible for correctness and safety. Check: if generated code looks polished, can it be deployed without inspection? No. Validate behavior, dependencies and security first.

scenes.title: Amazon Q Developer in IDE
scenes.narration: A development environment, often called an I D E, is an editor with tools for writing, navigating, debugging and testing software. Amazon Q Developer integrations historically offered suggestions and code review within development workflows. A developer could request help understanding a piece of code or ask for security findings. Treat the result as a review aid rather than a definitive security assessment. The lesson's product update matters: AWS ended Amazon CodeGuru Security support in November twenty twenty five, and the course notes say the Q Developer I D E plugins have a published end of support date of April thirtieth, twenty twenty seven. Supported integrations can change, so inspect current AWS documentation before choosing tooling for a new team. When a review warns about embedded credentials, insecure permissions or missing input validation, verify the finding and fix the code. Also check what the tool cannot detect. A model assisted review complements unit tests, code scanning and human security review; it does not replace them.
